summary: Removed domain-specific model names from executor failure injection to fix leakage objection.

edits.hypothesis: Removing specific model/tool names ('llava_med_qa', 'roi_crop') from the dynamic failure injection message eliminates task-specific leakage while preserving the core heuristic to re-examine original pixels after tool failure.
edits.why_not_lower_lever: The mechanism is a control-flow injection; the content of the injected message must be generic to pass the generalization litmus test, which a prompt-only edit cannot achieve if the injection logic itself contains hardcoded names.
edits.trigger_condition: When tool_failure_reason(obs) returns a non-None value in the executor loop.
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) The previous edit was rejected for leaking 'llava_med_qa' and 'roi_crop'. This edit removes those specific identifiers, replacing them with generic 'model outputs', allowing the same corrective mechanism to function without violating the no-leakage rule. (preservative) The instruction still forces re-examination of original pixels, preserving the success habit of visual verification. (transfer) Generalizes to any domain where a primary inspection tool fails and fallback models are used.
edits.regression_risk: Minimal; the message is only injected on failure and reinforces existing system prompt instructions without contradicting them.
edits.mechanism: Removing specific model/tool names ('llava_med_qa', 'roi_crop') from the dynamic failure injection message eliminates task-specific leakage while preserving the core heuristic to re-examine original pixels after tool failure.
